_why: M6 lab end state, read after "Commit the data-plane layer" and before "Teardown". SIMULATED is the one tag no part of the lab exceeds (Phase 6 CONTEXT D-36): the storage half runs real protocols on a real kind cluster and is scope-limited by three fences, and the device and the NIC are synthetic, published by two releases of the upstream example driver. Object state and record presence only (TRUST-06, STANDARDS.md C26, D-06, D-34): claim allocation results, a ResourceSlice attribute, an event by reason, a namespace's existence, and the presence of the learner's measurement record with its declared-environment block. No number in any record is read, and no Pod phase is read. Every kubectl runs with KUBECONFIG exported and --context kind-grid-core; every matches is anchored and in JavaScript regex dialect. Measurement directories named checkpoint-storm-* belong to the deep dive and are skipped here. Paths are relative to the learner tree (the labs repo root); in src run it from labs/ with: (cd labs && node ../scripts/run-checks.mjs m6/checks.json).

checks.describe: the lab's measurement record: in the newest measurement directory that is not a checkpoint-storm-* one, table-<RUN_ID>.md carries rows for all four paths (s3, nfs, pvc, hostpath) with none of them unmeasured, conclusion.md carries the five environment keys each with a value, and its Tier split: line names both the local and the network paths. No figure in either file is read (TRUST-06, C26, D-34). A missing record prints env=missing-record
checks.run: d=""; for x in grid-platform/dataplane-storage/measurements/*/; do case "$x" in */checkpoint-storm-*) continue ;; esac; [ -f "${x}conclusion.md" ] && d="$x"; done; [ -n "$d" ] || { echo "paths=0 env=missing-record conclusion=missing"; exit 0; }; t=""; for y in "$d"table-*.md; do [ -f "$y" ] && t="$y"; done; p=0; if [ -n "$t" ]; then for q in s3 nfs pvc hostpath; do r=$(grep -c "^| $q | [0-9]" "$t"); u=$(grep "^| $q |" "$t" | grep -c unmeasured); [ "${r:-0}" -ge 1 ] && [ "${u:-0}" -eq 0 ] && p=$((p+1)); done; fi; e=0; for k in "Host:" "Container runtime VM:" "Kubernetes:" "Other containers on the VM:" "Harness run id:"; do v=$(sed -n "s/^$k[[:space:]]*//p" "${d}conclusion.md" | head -1 | tr -d '[:space:]'); [ -n "$v" ] && e=$((e+1)); done; ts=$(sed -n 's/^Tier split:[[:space:]]*//p' "${d}conclusion.md" | head -1 | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'); c=missing; case "$ts" in *local*) case "$ts" in *network*) c=tier-split ;; esac ;; esac; if [ "$e" -eq 5 ]; then ev=declared; else ev="missing-$((5-e))"; fi; echo "paths=$p env=$ev conclusion=$c"

checks.describe: the harness configuration sits beside the figures it explains: the newest lab measurement directory holds harness-config.md, its Run id: value R is read, and table-R.md and results-R.jsonl are in the same directory (D-34). The run id is the harness's own; the directory name is the page's MEASURE_ID
checks.run: d=""; for x in grid-platform/dataplane-storage/measurements/*/; do case "$x" in */checkpoint-storm-*) continue ;; esac; [ -f "${x}harness-config.md" ] && d="$x"; done; [ -n "$d" ] || { echo "config=missing run_id=none"; exit 0; }; r=$(sed -n 's/^Run id: `\([^`]*\)`.*$/\1/p' "${d}harness-config.md" | head -1); [ -n "$r" ] || { echo "config=beside run_id=unreadable"; exit 0; }; if [ -f "${d}table-$r.md" ] && [ -f "${d}results-$r.jsonl" ]; then echo "config=beside run_id=match"; else echo "config=beside run_id=mismatch"; fi

checks.describe: both redirections held: git reports no change under storage/four-path (the committed harness-config.md is untouched) and no table-* or results-* file was written there. Without CONFIG_OUT and RESULTS_DIR the harness rewrites its own committed config (research Pitfall 11, threat T-06-37)
checks.run: [ -f storage/four-path/run.sh ] || { echo "harness_tree=absent"; exit 0; }; s=$(git status --porcelain -- storage/four-path 2>&1); n=0; for f in storage/four-path/table-* storage/four-path/results-*; do [ -e "$f" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; if [ -z "$s" ] && [ "$n" -eq 0 ]; then echo "harness_tree=clean"; else echo "harness_tree=dirty"; fi

checks.describe: the storage layer came down clients first: namespace spike-02 is absent, not Terminating. A namespace still Terminating is the hard-mount deadlock the teardown order exists to prevent (a measured Phase 1 finding). An unreadable namespace list prints unread, never absent
checks.run: export KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}"; j=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core get namespaces -o json 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$j" ] || { echo "storage_namespace=unread"; exit 0; }; s=$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r 'if (.items | length) == 0 then "unread" else ([.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "spike-02") | .status.phase] | if length == 0 then "absent" else "present-" + .[0] end) end'); echo "storage_namespace=${s:-unread}"

checks.describe: the synthetic-NIC driver's ResourceSlices, selected by spec.driver because the device driver's slices sit on the same node: four synthetic NICs, each publishing resource.kubernetes.io/pcieRoot. The NICs are synthetic, published by a second release of the upstream example driver
checks.run: export KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}"; kubectl --context kind-grid-core get resourceslices -o json | jq -r --arg d sim-nic.example.com --arg k resource.kubernetes.io/pcieRoot '[.items[] | select(.spec.driver == $d) | .spec.devices[]] as $n | "driver=" + (if ($n | length) > 0 then $d else "none" end) + " devices=" + ($n | length | tostring) + " pcieroot=" + ([$n[] | .attributes[$k].string | select(. != null and . != "")] | length | tostring)'

checks.describe: the claim named in Pod accel-and-nic's status.resourceClaimStatuses, in m6-network, holds two allocation results naming the two drivers: the synthetic device's and the synthetic NIC's. One claim, both allocated (SC4, D-27)
checks.run: export KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}"; c=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m6-network get pod accel-and-nic -o jsonpath='{.status.resourceClaimStatuses[0].resourceClaimName}' 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$c" ] || { echo "results=0 drivers=none"; exit 0; }; o=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m6-network get resourceclaim "$c" -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '(.status.allocation.devices.results // []) as $r | "results=" + ($r | length | tostring) + " drivers=" + ([$r[].driver] | sort | join(","))'); echo "${o:-results=0 drivers=unread}"

checks.describe: each of that claim's results (driver, pool, device) joined to its ResourceSlice's resource.kubernetes.io/pcieRoot: both results join, and the two roots are one root. A result that does not join prints unjoined, never a pass
checks.run: export KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}"; c=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m6-network get pod accel-and-nic -o jsonpath='{.status.resourceClaimStatuses[0].resourceClaimName}' 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$c" ] || { echo "roots=0 root=noclaim"; exit 0; }; s=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core get resourceslices -o json 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$s" ] || { echo "roots=0 root=unread"; exit 0; }; o=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m6-network get resourceclaim "$c" -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r --argjson s "$s" --arg k resource.kubernetes.io/pcieRoot '[(.status.allocation.devices.results // [])[] as $r | $s.items[] | select(.spec.driver == $r.driver and .spec.pool.name == $r.pool) | .spec.devices[] | select(.name == $r.device) | .attributes[$k].string // empty] as $roots | if ($roots | length) < 2 then "roots=0 root=unjoined" else ($roots | unique) as $u | "roots=" + ($u | length | tostring) + " root=" + ($u | join(",")) end'); echo "${o:-roots=0 root=unread}"

checks.describe: the deliberate failure: Pod split-roots's claim, from accel-and-nic-split-roots, has no .status.allocation, and the Pod carries a FailedScheduling event whose message says the scheduler cannot allocate all claims. Read from the claim and the event, never from the Pod's phase
checks.run: export KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}"; c=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m6-network get pod split-roots -o jsonpath='{.status.resourceClaimStatuses[0].resourceClaimName}' 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$c" ] || { echo "allocation=noclaim event=none"; exit 0; }; a=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m6-network get resourceclaim "$c" -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'if .status.allocation == null then "none" else "present" end'); n=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m6-network get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=split-roots,reason=FailedScheduling -o json 2>/dev/null | jq '[.items[] | select(.message | test("cannot allocate all claims"))] | length'); if [ "${n:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then e=FailedScheduling; else e=none; fi; echo "allocation=${a:-unread} event=$e"

checks.describe: the commit step: git tracks a lab measurement directory holding harness-config.md, table-*.md, results-*.jsonl and conclusion.md; storage/paths.md; the three network/ files (the claim template, the NIC driver's values copy, the class reference); and the six wrappers under addon-dataplane and addon-dra-nic, each of which, comment lines stripped, execs the single-source layer script of the same name
checks.run: m=no; for d in $(git ls-files grid-platform/dataplane-storage/measurements | sed -n 's#^\(grid-platform/dataplane-storage/measurements/[^/]*\)/.*#\1#p' | sort -u); do case "$d" in */checkpoint-storm-*) continue ;; esac; f=$(git ls-files "$d"); h=0; for pat in '/harness-config\.md$' '/table-[^/]*\.md$' '/results-[^/]*\.jsonl$' '/conclusion\.md$'; do c=$(printf '%s\n' "$f" | grep -c "$pat"); [ "${c:-0}" -ge 1 ] && h=$((h+1)); done; [ "$h" -eq 4 ] && m=yes; done; s=no; [ -n "$(git ls-files grid-platform/dataplane-storage/storage/paths.md)" ] && s=yes; n=0; for x in accel-and-nic-one-root.yaml sim-nic-values.yaml sim-nic-class.md; do [ -n "$(git ls-files "grid-platform/dataplane-storage/network/$x")" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; if [ "$n" -eq 3 ]; then nw=yes; else nw=no; fi; w=0; for pair in addon-dataplane:dataplane addon-dra-nic:dra-nic; do p=${pair%%:*}; l=${pair#*:}; for v in create verify teardown; do f="grid-platform/clusters/$p/$v.sh"; [ -n "$(git ls-files "$f")" ] || continue; c=$(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep -F "/clusters/grid-core/addons/$l/$v.sh" | grep -c '^exec '); [ "$c" = "1" ] && w=$((w+1)); done; done; echo "measurements=$m storage=$s network=$nw wrappers=$w"
